render_attempts.prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

At the same time, an active policy should not silently erase the provenance and alternatives needed by later policies to audit how the present state arose.
Future Janus faces receive no votes before they exist; their possibility is protected as a property of one continuing host.
A current face may change future world state but does not gain the power to gratuitously destroy the history through which a future Janus could understand itself.
HOLD is not universally safe: in a changing world, inaction can itself become an irreversible action.
An irreversible commit is admissible when it preserves more future agency than delay and does not erase causal lineage without necessity.
Memory may leave active access without turning forgetting into destruction of provenance.
